name: @projexlight/sdk-projection
summary: Identity Projection System (G4 closer): materialized per-(person, app, tenant) view of identity claims that every other SDK can sub-millisecond resolve against without joining live tables. Worker keeps the projection fresh from identity.* + tenant.* + persona.* deltas; projection_version on every claim envelope so consumers detect staleness. Foundation for the sub-ms identity hot path and any other denormalized canonical view downstream SDKs need.

events.name: projection.subject.refreshed.v1
events.description: A (person, app, tenant) row was rebuilt from upstream deltas; carries new projection_version.

events.name: projection.subject.stale.v1
events.description: Worker detected a stale row beyond the SLA window; consumed by the alerter.

events.name: projection.batch.completed.v1
events.description: Bulk catch-up completed (e.g. after a tenant-wide identity change).

models.description: Denormalized identity claims keyed by (person_id, app_id, tenant_id). Includes admin_pool_index, app_pool_index, current_membership_role, bu_id, projection_version, refreshed_at.

hooks.name: resolveSubject
hooks.description: Sub-ms lookup. Returns the full claims row or null. Used in the gateway hot path for every authenticated request.

hooks.name: enqueueRefresh
hooks.description: Tells the worker a specific (person_id, app_id, tenant_id) needs rebuilding; idempotent.

hooks.name: startProjector
hooks.description: Background worker that pulls inbox messages (from sdk-identity / sdk-tenant / sdk-persona) and rebuilds affected rows. Safe to leave running in dev.

hooks.name: inboxEnqueue
hooks.description: Called by upstream SDKs whenever something they own changes (registerPerson, attachReseller, createSubTenant, etc.) so the projector picks it up.

scenarios.title: Sub-ms identity resolve on every authenticated request
scenarios.when_to_use: The gateway hot path. After requireAuth validates the JWT, resolveSubject() pulls the full claim set so downstream SDKs don't have to re-join.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns the projected row in O(1) (typically <1ms with the Redis warm path). Null indicates the row hasn't been rebuilt yet — caller should enqueueRefresh + 503.

scenarios.title: Force-refresh after a role-template change
scenarios.when_to_use: Admin updates the role template for a tenant; we need affected subjects' projection rows rebuilt before the next request hits the cache.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Worker rebuilds each row on its next tick (within PROJECTION_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS). Emits projection.subject.refreshed.v1 per row with the new projection_version.

scenarios.title: Stale-row detector pages on-call when projection lag breaches SLA
scenarios.when_to_use: Production deployment. A stale row > 5s old in the gateway hot path is a Sev-2; the worker fires the alarm rather than the gateway returning incorrect claims.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Stale rows queue-jump to the next refresh tick. If lag persists, the projection_version on outgoing JWTs is forcibly bumped so consuming SDKs cache-miss + re-resolve.

scenarios.title: Bulk catch-up after a tenant-wide identity migration
scenarios.when_to_use: Operator runs a backfill (e.g. apply a new BU hierarchy across the tenant). Every projected row needs rebuild; we'd rather do it in one controlled pass than wait for inbox dribble.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Worker walks every (person, app) under the tenant, rebuilds each row, emits projection.batch.completed.v1 at end. New projection_version monotonically increases.

scenarios.title: sdk-identity enqueues into the inbox when a person registers
scenarios.when_to_use: Internal — every upstream identity write should land an inbox row so the projector picks it up. Documented here so downstream SDK authors know what to call.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Inbox row written; projector picks it up on its next tick; affected (person_id, *, *) projection rows rebuilt.

compliance_posture.notes: Projected rows are denormalized COPIES — source of truth lives in identity.* + tenant.*. GDPR right-to-erasure handled by sdk-data-rights walking the projection alongside the source tables. projection_version on every claim envelope lets consumers detect (and recover from) stale reads.

pricing_skus.unit_description: per resolve call (most are cached; cache misses billed at a higher rate)
per row rebuilt (background worker; rarely a hot SKU)
